incidents.victim: Telecom, Government, University, and Healthcare Sectors
incidents.vector: DLL sideloading via legitimate software packages (Poedit, curl, Vim, TightVNC) deployed post-compromise to establish long-term persistent access.
incidents.impact: NeedyMantis modular malware deployed against telecom organizations, universities, medical nonprofits, intergovernmental organizations, and government contractors in targeted intrusions dating to at least October 2025; enables long-term access, credential collection, and follow-on intelligence operations.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two critical zero-day remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772) in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances, both with CVSS 9.5.
incidents.impact: CISA confirmed global active exploitation and added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; more than 50,000 exposed instances identified. Federal agencies ordered to patch by September 30. Organizations may have been compromised before patches were available.

incidents.vector: Russian jet drone strike on Kyivstar's Kyiv headquarters, directly targeting the mobile provider's data center infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's largest mobile telecommunications provider suffered a direct kinetic strike on its data centers, disrupting mobile services for millions of Ukrainians.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273), the same vulnerability mass-exploited against dozens of organizations across healthcare, education, technology, and government; attackers bypassed Mandiant WAF mitigations via URL-encoding.
incidents.impact: Personal data on more than 5,000 FBI officials stolen, including Social Security numbers, duty assignments, psychiatric records, and medical files; stolen data shared with journalists, creating serious counterintelligence and agent safety risks. Attackers demanding the FBI retract a public advisory about their operations. Same campaign mass-exploited PeopleSoft across dozens of organizations in multiple sectors.

incidents.vector: Compromise of one of three hot wallet layers at the Singapore-based crypto trading platform.
incidents.impact: $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from Bitget's hot wallets — the largest crypto heist of 2026.

incidents.vector: Social engineering via WhatsApp and Telegram, impersonating known contacts or platform support; lure files disguised as legitimate apps (Norton Antivirus, Telegram, KeePass, medical documents) deploy CHOSEN BRICK malware.
incidents.impact: CHOSEN BRICK spyware deployed against regime critics in the UK, US, and Netherlands since at least 2025; enables screen capture, email and messaging theft, microphone access, and location tracking. Some victims' personal details published on pro-Iranian leak sites, increasing physical safety risk. UK NCSC, FBI, and Netherlands AIVD issued joint advisory.

incidents.vector: SQL injection vulnerability exploited in Medyc's web application interface in late August; an encrypted database archive was exfiltrated from Qbusoft's systems.
incidents.impact: Personal data of up to 5 million patients stolen, including names, national ID numbers, addresses, and likely psychiatric and medical records; the Addiction and Psychiatric Treatment Center in Inowrocław confirmed patients were affected. Poland's Central Bureau for Combating Cybercrime is investigating. The platform remains under repeated attack attempts.

incidents.vector: Coordinated distributed denial-of-service attacks against Norwegian public sector infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Key Norwegian government portals forced offline; Norwegian authorities characterized the campaign as a targeted effort to degrade national infrastructure in retaliation for Norway's military support for Ukraine.

incidents.vector: Unknown vulnerability exploited in MyDr's platform; attackers reportedly connected to same group behind the Medyc breach.
incidents.impact: Approximately 19 million patient records and data from roughly 12,000 healthcare organizations potentially exposed, including records linked to Poland's nationwide electronic health platform supporting electronic prescriptions and referrals.

incidents.victim: Pentagon / US Defense Manpower Data Center
incidents.vector: Misconfigured file-sharing system left exposed online without access controls for nearly nine months (October 2025 – July 2026).
incidents.impact: Names, military information, and Social Security numbers of Pentagon personnel exposed; unauthorized access confirmed during the exposure window. Pentagon has notified affected individuals.

incidents.vector: Compromised Azure service principal credentials (potentially from secrets exposed in a public GitHub issue edit history) used to conduct 15+ hours of reconnaissance followed by automated mass-deletion of cloud resources.
incidents.impact: More than 100 storage accounts, a Key Vault, Function App, App Service, and multiple Azure SQL databases deleted in a highly automated destruction campaign; backup and recovery controls were specifically targeted. No ransom note confirmed. Microsoft assessed the activity as consistent with ransomware or extortion operations.

incidents.vector: AI-generated deepfake voice impersonated Intesa Sanpaolo CEO in messages to Fideuram's chairman; a second AI voice clone impersonating a lawyer convinced an executive to approve fraudulent transactions routed to Chinese and Hong Kong bank accounts.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108M) stolen from Fideuram, Italy's largest private bank. Intesa Sanpaolo recovered more than half; €36 million remains missing.

incidents.vector: Social engineering — a Dutch-speaking attacker telephoned an Odido employee and tricked them into logging in at a spoofed website, yielding valid credentials.
incidents.impact: Personal data on 6.2 million Dutch people stolen. Dutch police arrested a suspected member in September 2026 in connection with the breach; the group has since escalated attacks in apparent retaliation.
